findings.title: A failed `changeset publish` leaves neither publishedPackages nor the changesets tag, so eql-assets throws on every push instead of repairing
findings.label: valid
findings.note: The cited code shows eqlAssets throws without thisRun or a changesets tag and eql-assets runs on every production push; changesets/action runs the publish via getExecOutput, which throws on a non-zero exit before outputs and tags are set, so the targeted repair can fail repeatedly.

findings.title: The npm listing wait times out or does not match what changesets reads, which blocks or still fails the JS release
findings.label: valid
findings.note: The new wait step throws at its 900 s deadline before changesets/action runs, holding the whole JS release until a re-run; this is a real, loud consequence of the change.

findings.title: Repair builds publish SQL and docs built from an older commit with today's toolchain under an already-released version
findings.label: valid
findings.note: Repair builds rebuild old source with head's workflow and a 'latest' Rust toolchain; AGENTS.md says nothing proves the rebuilt bytes match npm's, so a released SQL bundle or image could differ silently.
